title: [Bug]: transform hook sourcemap with relative `sources` resolved against process cwd instead of module directory
body:
### Reproduction link or steps

[REPL repro](https://repl.rolldown.rs/#)

Entry `index.js` imports `/lib/dep.js`; a `transform` plugin returns a map for it with relative `sources`: `./helper.ts` and `../shared/original.ts` (both relative to the module's own directory `/lib/`). Open the `index.js.map` output tab.

This is what happens in practice with `@rolldown/plugin-babel`: babel's default `inputSourceMap: true` makes it chain a prebuilt dependency's `//# sourceMappingURL` map, so the transform returns a multi-source map whose `sources` are relative to that dependency's own directory.

(Two sources are the minimum for a repro: a single-source map whose source differs from the module id is by design rewritten to the id itself.)

### What is expected?

```json
"sources": ["../lib/helper.ts", "../shared/original.ts"]
```

i.e. relative sources anchored at the module's directory, then relativized against the emitted map's location (`/dist/`).


### What is actually happening?

```json
"sources": ["../helper.ts", "../shared/original.ts"]
```

`./helper.ts` was anchored at the process cwd (`/`) instead of `/lib/`, losing the `lib` segment. (The second entry coincides either way in this flat layout, since `/` + `../shared/...` normalizes back to `/shared/...`.)

Any consumer resolving the emitted map against real files (error stack re-mapping, editor go-to-source) lands on a path that never existed.

### System Info

```Shell
System:
    OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200
    CPU: (24) x64 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700
    Memory: 1.07 GB / 63.68 GB
  Binaries:
    Node: 24.11.1 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE
    Yarn: 4.18.0 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\yarn.CMD
    npm: 11.17.0 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 152.0.7977.76
    Edge: Chromium (152.0.4191.53)
    Firefox: 136.0.4 - C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe
    Internet Explorer: 11.0.26100.8115
  npmPackages:
    rolldown: ^1.2.7 => 1.2.7
```

### Any additional comments?

Likely root cause: relative `sources` of a plugin-returned map are never anchored when the map enters the module's sourcemap chain; the output stage then absolutizes them against the process cwd. The `load` hook already anchors its maps this way since #765; `transform` has preserved multi-source maps since #2977 but never got the anchoring.

Note this has no Rollup counterpart to "match": Rollup discards a transform map's `sources` entirely and only traces `mappings` back to the module itself (verified: the same repro yields just `['lib/dep.js']` under Rollup). Since rolldown deliberately preserves them (#2977, motivated by rolldown-vite), their anchoring rule is rolldown's to define — reusing the load-side rule (`resolve(dirname(id), sourceRoot, source)`) keeps both hooks consistent.

I have a fix ready, a shared `rebase_sources_against_module_dir` helper applied as both `load`- and `transform`- returned maps enter the chain, replacing the now-duplicated JS-side `load` handling, plus a regression test that fails without it. Happy to open a PR.
